searches.note: Twenty five searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's, and three left unspent. Two were restricted to the house's own domain (gramona.com: III Lustros and La Plana, and its serving and tasting sheets) and are read as primary through their summaries; the rest went to the open web with the author's sources blocked where they would only have repeated themselves (the houses' own domains, Matthew Clark, Wikipedia, Decanter, Glass of Bubbly, Vinetur, Spanish Wine Lover, Squelch, Catalonia Today, Corpinnat's own site by turns). The two shared searches are Corpinnat's founders and rules, and the exit of Raventós i Blanc with the sales of 2018 to Carlyle and Henkell. One Freixenet search (Cordon Negro's year) found only bottles without a year and is counted. No fetch tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to independent accounts of each house's dates and people, then to the houses' own sheets for what only they can say, then to merchants' and importers' sheets for the making and the glass, with the author's sources blocked so that an independent account could be heard.

Where two accounts disagreed and neither was primary, the fact was cut or hedged as the house's; where a fact the author left out was now borne out twice (the Freixenet killings of the Civil War, the 1970's blend), it was added.

tested: 1551 and 1659, with the author's sources blocked: 15 Bodegas and Selectus Wines give the document of Jaume Codorníu's presses, barrels and vats of 1551 and Anna Codorníu's marriage to Miquel Raventós in 1659, the last of the family to bear the name; the library's 1551 agrees. Confirmed.

1872, the journey to Champagne and the grapes: DO Cava's own pages (the traditional method; the house's page on cava.wine) give the first bottles at Sant Sadurní in 1872 from Macabeo, Xarel·lo and Parellada; several accounts read through one summary (Grape Collective, Bkwine and others) give the visit to Champagne. One account has the son fix the three grape blend sixteen years later, so the grapes of 1872 are hedged as the house's account.

The son's taking charge in 1885, the cellars of Puig i Cadafalch from 1895 to 1915 and the monument of 1976: Arquitectura Catalana, Can Robira, 15 Bodegas and DO Cava's page for the house. Confirmed; the start year stays the 1890s (1902 by the Diputació).

Anna's launch in 1984 and the first Chardonnay Cava: the house's group page says 1984, the first Chardonnay Cava in history; Wikipedia's Cava article gives 1981 for the first Cava to use Chardonnay and one blog dates Anna to 1981. Hedged in the story and the card, cut from the table line.

The blend and the lees: importers' and merchants' sheets (Eynsham Cellars, Decántalo and others) give Chardonnay about seventy per cent with Parellada, Xarel·lo and Macabeo and at least fifteen months on the lees, a Brut. Confirmed; the Reserva stays untaught (see open).

Carlyle's majority of 2018 (about 68 per cent, by Hispanidad and Sivarious) and Raventós i Blanc's exit from DO Cava in 2012 (Quench, Sivarious, Grape Collective): confirmed. Puig i Cadafalch's dates, 1867 to 1956, are the Diputació's and stand. The house rules hold: nobody living named, no price, no score, British, no dash.

tested: 1861 and 1914, with the house's domains blocked: the International Directory of Company Histories (mirrored by Reference for Business and Encyclopedia.com) and Selectus Wines give Casa Sala of 1861 and the brand of 1914 from the farm La Freixeneda; the marriage year is told as 1889 or 1911, which the record does not give. Confirmed.
La Freixeneda's age: the thirteenth century on one account, the sixteenth on the International Directory's. Cut.

The Civil War and after: Spanish Wikipedia, the house's own obituary of 2024, Revista Enólogos and Tecnovino, read through one summary, give the co-founder's husband and an elder son killed at the start of the war, the co-founder at the head until her death and the daughters relaunching the house; the son who later led it joined in 1947, ran it from 1959 and presided from 1978, against the International Directory's 1957. Rewritten, with the year cut.

Cordon Negro: merchants give twelve to eighteen months on the lees, a dosage of about nine grams a litre and 6 to 8 degrees Celsius among the serving figures; the shared producer blurb gives apple, pear, citrus and a hint of ginger. The author's nine months to a year, nine grams, 6 to 8 degrees and the glass stand. The year 1974 was not found independently by the refuter (the search read only bottles without a year) and stands on the house's own page of the fiftieth year and the author's sources.

Henkell's majority of 2018: Sivarious and Aficionadovino give Henkell's majority since 2018 and a first structure called equal by one; kept as the author's majority. Cuvée D.S. named for the co-founder Dolors Sala: the house's own page and a trade interview. Confirmed. The house rules hold: the founders described, nobody living named, no price, no score, British, no dash.

III Lustros of 1951 and its release: 1951 by every account and the house's page of its seventy fifth year; 1961 by most, 1959 by one. Kept.

The lees and the cork: the house's sheet gives more than 84 months and its page more than 80; merchants' vintages run from 78 to 90 months; natural cork for wines aged more than five years by the house through Lebendige Weine. Confirmed.

La Plana and Font de Jui: the house's own pages give III Lustros from La Plana, part of what is now the Paraje Font de Jui, and Celler Batlle from the first vineyard the family owned. Confirmed; the blend of the 2017 sheet (Xarel·lo, Macabeo and a fifth Parellada) bears out the author's grapes.

The glass: the house's sheet gives white fruit, chamomile, brioche, breadcrumbs and dried apricot; worked in. Corpinnat's founding six and its rules (organic, hand picked, eighteen months, made on the estate) by Quench, The Drinks Business and Wein.plus, as the label term says. The house rules hold.

livingNote: None of these is named in the fragment's prose; the read together agent adds those it judges living to people.json (Gramona and Torres as the names of houses, which a house keeps). Josep Ferrer Sala, the Freixenet son who joined in 1947 and led the house from 1959, died on 5 November 2024 aged 99 by the house's own obituary, Revista Enólogos, Tecnovino and Tapas: he is not living and must not go on people.json; the record describes him as a younger son until his birth year is read in two sources. Long dead or undated and described, never named: Jaume Codorníu (1551), Anna Codorníu and Miquel Raventós (1659), Josep Raventós (1872, birth 1816 or 1824) and Manuel Raventós (1885); Francesc Sala Ferrés (1861), Dolors Sala and Pere Ferrer of Freixenet; Josep, Pau and Pilar Batlle, Bartomeu Gramona and his father Josep, and the brothers of the 1940s of Gramona; Josep Mata Capellades and Recaredo Mata Figueres; Jaume and Miquel Torres Vendrell (their dates differ by account). Named with dates and borne out: Josep Puig i Cadafalch (1867 to 1956) and Miguel Torres Carbó (1909 to 1991).
swapNote: No swap was proposed by the author, and the refuter proposes none. Codorníu and Freixenet are the two houses of Sant Sadurní every account of Cava begins with, each with the wine the plan names; Gramona and Recaredo are founding houses of Corpinnat (Quench, The Drinks Business), each with its long aged flagship; Familia Torres is the still wine house of the Penedès with the Cabernet whose 1970 placed first at the Olympiad of 1979.
planNotes: codorniu: answered. The label taught is Anna de Codorníu Blanc de Blancs, a Brut; the Reserva of the merchants' sheets is left untaught (open). The marriage of 1659 by 15 Bodegas and Selectus Wines with the author's two; the maker of 1872 not named, his birth year unsettled; the sale of a majority to Carlyle in 2018 by Hispanidad and Sivarious with the author's two, told with its year only.

freixenet: answered. 1914 with Casa Sala of 1861 by the International Directory and Selectus Wines; the families' story borne out, with the killings of the Civil War added; Cordon Negro's 1974 on the house's own page and the author's three; Henkell's majority of 2018 by Sivarious and Aficionadovino with the author's two; no living member named.

gramona: answered. Cava Gran Reserva Brut Nature before 2019 and Corpinnat Brut Nature since, by the house and merchants; more than eighty months under cork by the house (more than 84 on its sheet). The why's 1881 and very long lees ageing of Xarel·lo stand; no living member named.

recaredo: answered. 1924 by three accounts; the founder's dates not found, so he is described; the planting of 1940 by Decanter and MundoVinum; the lees more than a hundred months by the house; a founder of Corpinnat by Quench and The Drinks Business. The why's every wine disgorged by hand stands; without freezing is the house's account (open).

torres: answered. The 1970 as Gran Coronas Black Label, the Olympiad of 1979 and the name Mas La Plana from the 1990s (the 1995 vintage by Decanter); Grans Muralles and Milmanda kept as Conca de Barberà wines by the library; no living member named. The why's put Penedès reds on lists abroad is the house's and the Decanter legend's reading and stands as the plan's.
